taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: An annual: grown for its one season, as the library's annual herbs are.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.note: By eye from the photos (observations 33236284, 133248955, 324238842, 238154280, 238508458, 143912946, 7484484, 17786628): a small, loosely branched annual tuft of few short blades and slender culms, each ending in a zigzag axis of pale straw, needle-like spikes that hang down and fall whole. The panicle's colour comes from flower_colour through the family's rule, its spikelets from the order's.

traits.life_span.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: annual, erect or spreading, branching.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: culms slender, 10 to 30 cm tall.

traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: culms slender, 10 to 30 cm tall.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: annual, from fibrous roots.

traits.clonal.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: annual.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: blades small and few, in vigorous plants as much as 15 cm long; 1 cm to 5 cm usual (species-facts estimate).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 1 mm to 2 mm wide.

traits.inflorescence.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: spikes mostly 8 to 14 on a slender axis, reflexed, readily falling: a panicle of short spikes.

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: spikes mostly 8 to 14 on a slender axis.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the axis with its spikes 3 cm to 8 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.florets_per_spikelet.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: spikelets 2 to 4, narrow, appressed; rudiment of 3 scabrous awns exceeding the fertile floret: one fertile floret.

traits.awns.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: rudiment of 3 scabrous awns about 5 mm long, exceeding the fertile floret.

traits.awn_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 512, Bouteloua aristidoides: rudiment of 3 scabrous awns about 5 mm long.

traits.awn_insertion.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the awns leave the floret's tip.

traits.fruit_type.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a grain (caryopsis), as in every grass.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles, Flowering Plants and Ferns of Arizona (1942) p. 138, Bouteloua aristidoides: deserts, dry mesas, and rocky hillsides, June to October; the summer-rain months July to October drawn.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: grains ripe August to November.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for needle grama from Hitchcock (1935 p. 512): an annual, erect or spreading and branching (tillers 10, tiller_lean 30), culms slender (culm_radius 0.0006), blades small and few (leaves 2), spikes reflexed on a slender axis; grown and flowering in its one year (adult_age 1, maturity 0.3), set by hand as the poaceae program's own adult_age would otherwise hold it back a year.

allometry.note: 0.2 m tall at 1 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
